title: Luang Prabang Half Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2025 Race Was Like
seo_title: Luang Prabang Half Marathon Review: Loops, Weather, Rules, Field
meta_description: Luang Prabang Half Marathon review: 3,000+ runners in 2025 on loops of the old town from the Royal Palace, 21°C and 100% humidity at 7am, a 3h30 road closure, and how small the 21 km field is.
dek: What the Run for Children in Luang Prabang is like, from the 2025 edition: a charity race on 7 km loops of the old-town peninsula, a mild but saturated dawn, roads that reopen after three and a half hours, and a half-marathon field of under 200 finishers.
verdict: Enter if you want a small, friendly charity race through a heritage town, where the cause and the dawn setting matter more than the clock. The 2025 race drew more than 3,000 runners, most of them on the 7 km, starting from the Royal Palace with the monks' alms round under way. At 7am it was 21°C with 100% humidity: mild for the region, but sticky. The catches are the roads and the format. The course is loops of the peninsula, the roads reopen after three and a half hours, and a runner in 2019 had to cross live traffic after the first loop. Run without music, and aim to finish well inside the limit.

sections.heading: The 2025 Race: A Hospital Fundraiser in the Old Town
paragraphs: The Run for Children Luang Prabang Half Marathon 2025 was held on Saturday 25 October and drew more than 3,000 participants, according to China Daily and the Laotian Times [1][2]; the Chinese consulate in Luang Prabang, whose staff ran the 7 km, put the field at more than 2,800, a record for the event [3]. The year before, more than 2,400 people from 53 countries took part [4].

The race began at the National Museum, the former Royal Palace, and passed temples along the Mekong and Nam Khan rivers; the monks' morning alms ceremony took place outside the palace during the race [1]. The 21 km started at 5.30am, the 14 km at 5.45am and the 7 km at 6.00am, with the start and finish near the Royal Palace Museum [5]. The organiser times the start so runners can see the alms round on their first lap [6].

It is a fundraiser first. The race began in 2013, and since 2016 the Lao Friends Hospital for Children has owned it; the organiser says all the money raised goes to the hospital's free healthcare for more than 30,000 patients a year [6]. The rules name the hospital and Events For Good as organisers [7], and Tigerhead drinking water has been the platinum sponsor for 11 years [2].

sections.heading: The Course: Laps of the Peninsula
paragraphs: The organiser's FAQ explains the design: the aim was to keep the race on the peninsula, run along the riverside and pass as many UNESCO-protected buildings and temples as possible, and the longest loop that allowed was 7 km, so three circuits make a half marathon [6]. That is also why there is no 10 km or full marathon; the organiser says a marathon would mean six repetitive loops and longer road closures [6]. The 2024 timing points fit that design: the 21 km was timed at 2.3 km, 9.3 km and 16.3 km, exactly 7 km apart [8].

The route maps posted for 2026 show a different 21 km layout, split into a start-to-11 km section and a 12 km-to-finish section, passing Haw Pha Bang, Wat Xieng Thong, Wat Manorom and Wat Phone Sa Ath, with a stretch on Phetsarat Road [9]. The 2025 route map could not be found, so check the 2026 map rather than relying on older race reports.

Expect some undulation. A runner at the 2019 race described gentle inclines and downward slopes, and crowds of cheering schoolchildren and bar owners offering trays of drinks [10]. Another 2019 runner found the route went through housing estates, and thought it had fewer standout heritage sights than the Angkor Wat Half Marathon [11].

sections.heading: The Weather: Mild but Saturated
paragraphs: Luang Prabang airport, about 3 km east of the Royal Palace, has no readings before 7am, 90 minutes after the 21 km start. At 7am on race morning it recorded 21°C, a dew point of 21°C, 100% humidity and a 2-knot wind; 22°C and 94% at 8am; and 23°C and 89% at 9am [12]. By 10am it was 25°C [12].

Air at 21°C is mild for a Southeast Asian race, but with the dew point equal to the temperature, sweat barely evaporates. A runner in 2016 called the morning hot, muggy and smoky from the fires locals use for cooking and burning rubbish [13]. The organiser holds the race in October, at the end of the rainy season, and starts early because dawn is the coolest part of the day [6].

sections.heading: Roads, Aid and Cut-offs
paragraphs: The rules close the route to traffic for up to three and a half hours; after that the roads reopen to live traffic [7]. For a 5.30am start, that matches the 9am cut-off printed on the 2026 21 km map; the 14 km map gives 8.30am and the 7 km 8.00am [9]. In 2024 the slowest of the 183 half-marathon finishers took 3:25:38 [8].

Traffic is the main thing runners mention. A 2019 reviewer said that after the first loop, at about 14 km, the roads were reopened and runners had to watch for cars and cross junctions on their own, and advised not running with music [11]. A 2016 runner described cars, pickups, scooters and bicycles on the course, and weaving through traffic with three kilometres to go [13]. At the 2019 race, expat residents were out redirecting rickshaws [10].

Aid was not a complaint: the 2019 reviewer found the road signs adequate and had no complaints about the water points, which served water and isotonic drinks [11]. The 2026 map shows water every 2 km, with first-aid points at the even-numbered kilometre markers [9]. In 2016, 21 km runners had to cross the finish line on the right-hand side, which one runner nearly missed [13].

sections.heading: Rules Worth Knowing
paragraphs: You must start within 30 minutes of your flag-off or be disqualified [7]. Half marathoners must be at least 16 on race day and 14 km runners over 12; wheelchairs are allowed on the 7 km only [7]. There are no refunds for any reason, including cancellation of the event, no transfers and no changes of distance [7]. The race pack holds the bib, timing chip and event T-shirt, and finishers get a medal and an e-certificate [7].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: No results for 2025 could be found. In 2024, the most recent results published, the 21 km had 183 finishers, 136 men and 47 women [8]. Issei Kunihiro won in 1:24:14, leading a Japanese top three, and Liu Ye won the women's race in 1:39:06, ninth overall; tenth place was 1:41:53 for men and 2:03:16 for women [8]. Lao runners were the largest group of 21 km finishers, followed by Thai and Japanese runners [8].

The shorter races are where the numbers are: 232 finished the 14 km and 1,583 the 7 km in 2024, most of them Lao [8]. A sub-1:40 half marathon would have put you in the top ten overall. Trophies go to the top three in each age category, and there is no prize money [7].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: For 2026, international entries cost US$60 for the 21 km, US$45 for the 14 km and US$30 for the 7 km, and race kits are collected at Luang Prabang Preschool on 22 and 23 October, 10am to 6pm [14]. Lao nationals pay a local rate and must show ID at kit pick-up [6].

Luang Prabang has direct international flights from Hanoi, Siem Reap, Bangkok and some Chinese cities; otherwise fly to Vientiane and connect by domestic flight or the high-speed train [6]. A 2019 runner took a taxi of about 15 minutes from the airport, recommended staying in the town centre within walking distance of the start, and found race-pack collection went very smoothly [11].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a charity race in a small heritage town, run at dawn past temples and the alms procession, with a choice of one, two or three laps. It suits first-timers and families on the 7 km, and runners who want a relaxed half marathon with a place in their age group within reach.
Think twice if you want a fast, fully closed course or a big half-marathon field. Plan to finish well inside three and a half hours, and stay alert to traffic once the roads reopen.

The 2026 race is on Saturday 24 October [14]. The 2025 results and the 2025 route map have not been published anywhere found, and the 2026 map and registration page disagree on the 14 km start (5.30am or 5.45am) [9][14], so confirm start times with the organiser.

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's FAQ, rules, route maps and registration pages, news reports in English and Chinese, a tour operator's race listing, airport weather records, the 2024 results and three runners' accounts of earlier editions.

faqs.question: Why is there no 10 km at the Luang Prabang Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Because the course is built on laps. The organiser wanted to stay on the old-town peninsula, and the longest loop that allowed was 7 km, so the race offers 7 km, 14 km and 21 km, one, two or three laps. It suggests 10 km runners step up to the 14 km instead.

faqs.question: What time does the Luang Prabang Half Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Early. In 2025 the 21 km started at 5.30am, the 14 km at 5.45am and the 7 km at 6.00am, all from the Royal Palace. The start is timed so runners see the monks' alms round on their first lap. The 2026 map lists the 14 km at 5.30am, so check.

faqs.question: How hot is the Luang Prabang Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Mild but humid. At 7am on race morning in 2025, Luang Prabang airport recorded 21°C, a 21°C dew point and 100% humidity, rising to 23°C and 89% by 9am. A runner at an earlier edition described the morning as hot, muggy and smoky from cooking fires.

faqs.question: Are the roads closed for the Luang Prabang Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Only for up to three and a half hours; after that they reopen to traffic. A runner in 2019 said cars were back on the course after the first loop, at about 14 km, and advised running without music. Aim to finish well inside the limit and watch for vehicles.

faqs.question: How many people run the Luang Prabang Half Marathon 21 km?
faqs.answer: Fewer than 200. The 2025 event drew more than 3,000 participants, but in 2024, the latest published results, only 183 finished the 21 km, against 232 on the 14 km and 1,583 on the 7 km. A sub-1:40 half marathon was a top-ten finish.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 to the race-review template. Written about the previous edition (25 October 2025). No 2025 results or 2025 route map could be found, and the Wayback Machine was offline; the 2024 results are used for field depth, labelled as 2024, and the route is described from the organiser's FAQ, the 2024 timing points and the maps posted for 2026. Weather is from airport METAR observations, which start at 7am; not a forecast. Field size: more than 3,000 (China Daily, Laotian Times) versus more than 2,800 (Chinese consulate); both given. The 2026 map and registration page disagree on the 14 km start time. Runner accounts are from 2019 and 2016; none of the 2025 race was found. Facebook and Instagram could not be read. No rating.
